resumen: Lowering on one foot with the other leg straight in front. It asks for strength, balance and hip in equal parts.
ejecucion: Stand on one foot with the other leg straight in front and your arms forward.
Lower by bending the supporting knee and pushing the hip back.
Go as low as you can control, without letting the knee fall inwards.
Come up pushing through the whole foot, without a jerk.
If you cannot manage it yet, do it sitting to a bench or holding on to something.
matices: In the cited work, the single-leg squat produced more gluteus medius activation than the forward lunge or the lateral step-up: that is the price of holding the pelvis over one support. This is why it is so widely used to spot and fix the knee collapsing inwards.
